about.title: Walnut Creek Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: When you go in for care in Walnut Creek, you expect to come out better, not worse. But in a city of nearly 69,000 people, with residents traveling in from across Contra Costa County for appointments, surgeries, and follow-up visits, errors do occur, and the people they land on are often left with more questions than answers. Medical malpractice in California has its own rulebook, known as MICRA. It sets short deadlines, requires a formal notice before a lawsuit can be filed, and places a cap on non-economic damages that adjusts upward every year. It also demands proof, almost always through a qualified medical expert, that a provider fell below the accepted standard of care. A disappointing result on its own does not meet that bar. Our team handles medical malpractice cases for Walnut Creek residents. There is no charge for an initial consultation, and we work on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Walnut Creek Residents Choose Us for Malpractice Cases

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people think
items.desc: California generally allows one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. An early conversation helps you avoid losing a claim on timing alone.

items.title: The 90-day notice is handled correctly
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed, the provider must receive a formal notice of intent at least 90 days ahead. Our team is familiar with this step and how it interacts with the deadline.

items.title: Expert review comes first
items.desc: Almost every California malpractice case needs a qualified medical expert to explain how the standard of care was breached. We can arrange that review so you know early whether a claim is realistic.

items.question: I had a bad surgical result in Walnut Creek. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Medicine carries risk, and a poor outcome by itself does not prove negligence under California law. What matters is whether the provider did something a reasonably careful professional would not have done, or failed to do something they should have. A medical expert typically has to confirm that before a case moves forward.

items.question: I was treated in Walnut Creek but live in another part of Contra Costa County. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It usually does not affect whether you have a claim, though it can influence where a case is filed and which records need to be gathered. Contra Costa County cases are commonly heard in the county's superior court regardless of which city the treatment happened in. We can sort out the venue question quickly once we know the details.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in medical malpractice cases, and that cap increases every year under MICRA. Economic losses, including medical bills and lost income, are not subject to the same cap. We can explain how the current figures apply to your situation without anyone promising a specific result.
